Building nodes and packages
A ROS 2 workspace is a build boundary containing packages. A package is the unit of organization and dependency declaration; nodes are runtime participants implemented inside packages. colcon builds the workspace, while ament_cmake and ament_python provide the common C++ and Python package conventions.

3 modules 5 direct tutorials


Foundations: the ROS 2 graph
ROS 2 applications are graphs of independently useful nodes. Nodes exchange typed data through topics, request bounded work through services, run longer goal-oriented work through actions, and expose configuration through parameters. The command-line tools let you inspect this graph before writing code, which makes them the best starting point.
3 modules 6 direct tutorials


Interfaces, parameters, actions, and plugins
Interfaces are the public contracts between nodes. Messages describe topic samples, services pair a request with a response, and actions combine a goal, feedback, a result, and cancellation. Parameters configure a node but should not be mistaken for a high-rate data channel. Pluginlib adds runtime-selected implementations behind a stable C++ interface.

Middleware, discovery, and performance
ROS 2 client libraries communicate through an RMW abstraction over supported middleware implementations. Behavior depends on QoS compatibility, discovery, serialization, executor scheduling, process boundaries, memory allocation, and the network. Performance work therefore needs measurements and an explicit operating context.
